## Summary

Phase E — the **final piece** of the Parent Songbooks work. Closes out #782 by giving callers a clean programmatic surface for family / series queries AND automating the curator-side ergonomics of bulk-linking 22+ vernacular hymnals to their canonical parent after a scrape + bulk-import.

Closes **#782 phase E** (and with it, the whole #782).

## What's in this PR

### `SongData` — three new public helpers

- **`getSongbookFamily(string $abbr): array`** — returns `{ self, parent, children, siblings }` walking the `ParentSongbookId` FK in both directions. Pre-migration safe via the cached `_songbookParentSelect` probe.

- **`getSongbooksInSeries(int|string $idOrSlug): array`** — returns the songbooks that belong to a series, ordered by `SortOrder` then `Name`. Accepts either the int id or the URL-safe slug — handy for `/series/<slug>` public pages when those land.

- **`getSongCounterparts(string $songId): array`** — given a `SongId`, returns the same hymn-number's row in the parent songbook + every sibling translation/edition. Three queries total (probe + family walk + IN-list); empty for unnumbered songs, songbooks with no parent, or rows where no related songbook carries the same number.

### `ChristInSong.app.py` — manifest emission

After a successful scrape the script writes `_family-manifest.json` at the top of the output directory listing every vernacular hymnal as a translation child of the English CIS parent. Schema is versioned (`schema_version: 1`) and shaped so future scrapers (Mission Praise editions, Songs of Fellowship volumes-as-series) can write multi-family manifests on the same contract:

```json
{
  \"schema_version\": 1,
  \"scraper\": \"ChristInSong.app.py\",
  \"scraper_version\": \"1.0\",
  \"generated_at\": \"2026-05-02T...Z\",
  \"families\": [
    {
      \"parent\": { \"abbreviation\": \"CIS\", \"name\": \"Christ in Song\", \"language\": \"en\" },
      \"children\": [
        { \"abbreviation\": \"HA\", \"name\": \"Himnario Adventista\", \"language\": \"es\", \"relationship\": \"translation\" },
        ...
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

`--no-manifest` opts out. The manifest is skipped when CIS itself wasn't part of the run or failed (children would dangle).

### `/manage/songbooks` — Apply family manifest uploader

Admin / global_admin only. Curators upload the JSON above; the page parses + matches every `(parent, child)` pair against `tblSongbooks` and renders a preview table:

- **`will_link`** — child has no parent → set parent
- **`will_relink`** — child links elsewhere → only applied with a second \"Relink existing\" tick (destructive overwrite gate)
- **`already_ok`** — already correct → skipped
- **`parent_miss`** / **`child_miss`** — referenced row not in the catalogue → logged + skipped
- **`self`** — manifest claims child === parent → defensive skip

Two-step flow (preview → confirm + re-upload) keeps the destructive bits behind explicit ticks. Apply step runs in one transaction; success emits a `songbook.family_manifest_apply` activity-log row with the applied / skipped counts.

## Pre-migration safety

Every schema-touching path is gated by `INFORMATION_SCHEMA` probes for `ParentSongbookId` / `tblSongbookSeries`. A deployment that hasn't run `migrate-parent-songbooks.php` (#782 phase A) sees the helpers return empty shapes and the admin uploader rejects with a friendly \"schema not installed\" error.

## Files

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `appWeb/public_html/includes/SongData.php` | Three new public methods (~345 LOC). |
| `appWeb/public_html/manage/songbooks.php` | New `family_manifest` POST action + uploader card + preview table. |
| `.importers/scrapers/ChristInSong.app.py` | New `write_family_manifest()` + `--no-manifest` flag + call wired into `main()`. |

## Test plan

### Programmatic helpers

- [ ] On a populated DB with at least one parent-child relationship, call `\$songData->getSongbookFamily('CIS')` from a test harness or `php -r`. Expect `self`, `parent` (null for the canonical row), `children` (every linked vernacular), `siblings` (empty for the parent).
- [ ] Same helper on a vernacular abbreviation (e.g. `HA`). Expect `parent` populated and `siblings` listing the other vernaculars.
- [ ] On an unrelated standalone songbook (e.g. `MP`). Expect empty `parent` / `children` / `siblings`.
- [ ] Pre-migration: drop `tblSongbooks.ParentSongbookId` on a scratch DB. Same calls return the empty shape, no errors.
- [ ] `getSongbooksInSeries('songs-of-fellowship')` returns volume rows ordered by `SortOrder`. Same call with the int id returns the same list.
- [ ] `getSongCounterparts('HA-0042')` returns `parent` (CIS-0042 if it exists) + `siblings` (KMK-0042, KP-0042, etc. for every CIS sibling that carries number 42). Empty for `HA-0000` (unnumbered) and for `MP-0042` (no parent).

### Scraper manifest emission

- [ ] Run `python3 .importers/scrapers/ChristInSong.app.py --hymnal english,tswana,sotho` (a small subset). Expect `_family-manifest.json` at the top of `.SourceSongData/` with KMK + KP under CIS.
- [ ] `--no-manifest` skips the file.
- [ ] Run `--hymnal tswana,sotho` (no parent). Expect a console note and no manifest written.

### Admin uploader

- [ ] As an admin, open `/manage/songbooks`. Expect a new \"Apply family manifest\" card between the Auto-colour panel and the Create form.
- [ ] Upload `_family-manifest.json` with **Confirm** unticked. Expect a preview table with one row per `(parent, child)`. Rows where the child has no parent yet get `will_link` (info badge); rows already pointing at the right parent get `already_ok` (success badge).
- [ ] Re-upload with **Confirm** ticked. Expect the `will_link` rows to flip to `linked` and the songbook's Parent column on the list above to update on next page load.
- [ ] Manually set one child to point at a different parent via the edit modal. Re-upload. Expect that row to surface as `will_relink` (warning badge) and skip on apply unless **Relink existing** is also ticked.
- [ ] Upload a manifest that references a non-existent parent. Expect `parent_miss` for every child + the apply step skipping all of them.
- [ ] Pre-migration check: drop `ParentSongbookId`, reload `/manage/songbooks`. Expect the uploader to render but to reject the upload with \"schema not installed — run /manage/setup-database\".

### Activity log

- [ ] Apply a manifest. Expect a `songbook.family_manifest_apply` row in `/manage/activity-log` with `applied`, `skipped`, `plan_size`, and `relink_existing` fields.

## Refs

- Closes #782 phase E. With this merged, **the whole #782 is done.**
- Builds on the full chain: PR #790 (schema) → #799 (hierarchical admin UI) → #800 (series CRUD + membership picker) → #801 (public surfaces). No further migrations needed.

Phase A (schema) shipped on 2026-05-01 in PR #790 (commit 531ef33 on alpha). Phase B (hierarchical-parent admin UI) merged on 2026-05-02 in PR #799 (commit 77530fb on alpha) — adds the parent picker on the edit modal, a Parent column on the list view, the `parent_search` typeahead endpoint, and a server-side cycle guard (`_wouldCreateParentCycle` in `appWeb/public_html/manage/songbooks.php`). Phase C (peer-to-peer series CRUD + membership picker) merged on 2026-05-02 in PR #800 (commit bbd0af8 on alpha) — `/manage/songbook-series` page + checkbox group on the songbook edit modal. Phase D (public read surfaces) opened on 2026-05-02 in PR #801 against alpha — extends `SongData::getSongbook` / `getSongbooks` with probe-gated `parent` + `series` keys, adds `findSongIdByNumber` for deep-linking; renders a canonical-source link on the song page header and a "Part of: <Series>" line on songbook tiles in `home.php` / `songbooks.php`.

**Why:** Three real songbook families don't fit the flat `tblSongbooks` model:
1. **Christ in Song** — English `CIS` is canonical; the 22 vernacular hymnals from `ChristInSong.app.py` are translations sharing the same numbering map.
2. **Mission Praise** — multiple historical editions where the same hymn can carry different numbers.
3. **Songs of Fellowship** — multi-volume series where each volume is uniquely numbered (no cross-volume numbering).

**The lock-in (decided in #782 comment 4362114785):** two complementary shapes that coexist on a single row.

- **Hierarchical** (canonical-root case): self-FK on `tblSongbooks`:
  - `ParentSongbookId INT UNSIGNED NULL` (FK → tblSongbooks(Id), ON DELETE SET NULL)
  - `ParentRelationship ENUM('translation','edition','abridgement') NULL`
  - Use for: Spanish CIS → English CIS, MP2 → MP1, Children's MP → MP.
- **Peer-to-peer** (no-canonical-root case): two new tables `tblSongbookSeries` + `tblSongbookSeriesMembership`. Use for: Songs of Fellowship vols 1–4, themed compilations.
- A row can carry both — e.g. MP2 has `ParentSongbookId = MP1` AND a series membership row pointing to a "Mission Praise" series.

Migration: `appWeb/.sql/migrate-parent-songbooks.php` (idempotent, INFORMATION_SCHEMA-probed), wired into `/manage/setup-database` as action key `parent-songbooks` ("3x." card).

**How to apply:**
- When asked about parent/umbrella songbooks, point at PR #790 and #782 for context — the schema is in place but nothing reads or writes it yet.
- Pending phases tracked in #782, each its own PR:
  - ~~**B** — Admin UI: parent picker on songbook edit modal + cycle prevention.~~ (PR #799, merged on alpha 2026-05-02.)
  - ~~**C** — Admin UI: `/manage/songbook-series` CRUD + multi-select on edit modal.~~ (PR #800, merged on alpha 2026-05-02.)
  - ~~**D** — Public surfaces: song-page "original / canonical" badge; tile "part of `<series>`" line.~~ (PR #801, open against alpha 2026-05-02. Note: `/series/<slug>` route doesn't exist yet — series names render as plain text on tiles.)
  - **E** — Programmatic helpers (`SongData::getSongbookFamily`, `getSongbookSeries`) + bulk-import auto-link (e.g. ChristInSong.app.py scraper auto-linking the 22 vernaculars to the English CIS parent).
- The ChristInSong.app.py scraper still writes 22 sibling folders under `.SourceSongData/` — auto-linking on import is phase E, not in the scraper itself.
- Note the ENUM landed as `('translation','edition','abridgement')` — issue #782's original proposal said `'volume'` instead of `'abridgement'`, but volumes use the series tables, not the ENUM. Don't reinstate `'volume'`.

content.text:
Perfect! Now I have all the information. Let me write a comprehensive report.

---

## FINDINGS

**A. THE SIGNUP HTTP ENDPOINT**

**Server-side handler:** `/tmp/ihymns-signup/appWeb/public_html/api.php`, lines 791–951, case `auth_register`

**Error response pattern:**
- Returns JSON body with status code 4xx (400, 409, 403, 429 depending on the error)
- Format: `{"error": "User-facing message"}` 
- For invalid username specifically: **400 Bad Request** + `{"error": "Username must be at least 3 characters (letters, numbers, _, -, . only)."}`

**Username validation (line 862):**
```php
if (strlen($username) < 3 || !preg_match('/^[a-z0-9_.\-]+$/', $username)) {
    sendJson(['error' => 'Username must be at least 3 characters (letters, numbers, _, -, . only).'], 400);
    break;
}
```

The regex `/^[a-z0-9_.\-]+$/` explicitly rejects spaces. A username like `"ivan woodman"` (after `strtolower()`) fails this regex and returns the 400 error above.

---

**B. THE CLIENT-SIDE SIGNUP FORM**

**File:** `/tmp/ihymns-signup/appWeb/public_html/js/modules/user-auth.js`

**"Network error" string emitted at:** Lines 178 and 205 (in the `register()` method's catch block)

```javascript
async register(username, password, displayName) {
    try {
        const res = await fetch(`${this.app.config.apiUrl}?action=auth_register`, {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ... },
            body: JSON.stringify({ username, password, display_name: displayName }),
        });
        const data = await res.json();
        if (!res.ok) return { success: false, error: data.error || 'Registration failed.' };
        // ... success path ...
    } catch {
        return { success: false, error: 'Network error. Please try again.' };  // LINE 178
    }
}
```

**Condition that triggers "Network error":** Only a **JavaScript exception** in the try block (e.g., JSON parse failure, fetch network failure, CORS error). Non-2xx HTTP responses are handled gracefully—the code extracts `data.error` from the JSON response and returns it. The "Network error" message fires ONLY on a true exception, not on a 400/409 from the server.

**Form submission handler (lines 1229–1273):**
- Gets trimmed username from input: `username = modal.querySelector('#auth-username')?.value.trim()`
- Calls `this.register(username, password, displayName)`
- Displays the returned error: `errorEl.textContent = result.error`

Therefore:
- If server returns `{"error": "Username must be at least..."}` with 400, the client displays that exact string.
- Only if the fetch throws an exception does "Network error. Please try again." appear.

---

**C. USERNAME VALIDATION**

**Server-side:** Spaces in usernames are **explicitly rejected** by the regex at line 862 of api.php. The input `"Ivan Woodman"` becomes `"ivan woodman"` after `mb_strtolower(trim())` and fails the pattern `/^[a-z0-9_.\-]+$/`, triggering the 400 error.

**Client-side:** The `<input>` field has no pattern, maxlength, or client-side validation. Spaces are accepted in the form and sent to the server.

---

**D. ACTIVITY LOG**

The server logs successful registrations (line 928, `logActivity('auth.register', ...)`), but **validation failures (username with space, short password, etc.) are NOT logged to tblActivityLog**—the handler just calls `sendJson()` and breaks. Only a successful registration creates an audit entry.

---

**THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE USER'S ISSUE**

When the user enters `"Ivan Woodman"` as the username:
1. Client trims it to `"Ivan Woodman"` and sends it as JSON to `auth_register`
2. Server lowercases and trims it: `"ivan woodman"`
3. Server regex `/^[a-z0-9_.\-]+$/` rejects the space
4. Server returns **HTTP 400 + JSON body: `{"error": "Username must be at least 3 characters (letters, numbers, _, -, . only)."}`**
5. Client receives 400 (not-ok), extracts `data.error`, displays it in the modal

**The user should see:** "Username must be at least 3 characters (letters, numbers, _, -, . only)."

**But they report seeing:** "Network error. Please try again."

This suggests either:
- The fetch is throwing an **exception** before hitting the JSON parse (CORS failure, network timeout, 0-byte response)
- The server is not returning a valid JSON body on the 400 (client's `res.json()` throws)
- An iOS Safari-specific issue is silently failing the request

The regex validation is correct and intentional—the real bug is why the error is not reaching the UI as the server error message.

**Username validation (line 862):**
```php
if (strlen($username) < 3 || !preg_match('/^[a-z0-9_.\-]+$/', $username)) {
    sendJson(['error' => 'Username must be at least 3 characters (letters, numbers, _, -, . only).'], 400);
    break;
}
```

The regex `/^[a-z0-9_.\-]+$/` explicitly rejects spaces. A username like `"ivan woodman"` (after `strtolower()`) fails this regex and returns the 400 error above.

---

**B. THE CLIENT-SIDE SIGNUP FORM**

**File:** `/tmp/ihymns-signup/appWeb/public_html/js/modules/user-auth.js`

**"Network error" string emitted at:** Lines 178 and 205 (in the `register()` method's catch block)

```javascript
async register(username, password, displayName) {
    try {
        const res = await fetch(`${this.app.config.apiUrl}?action=auth_register`, {
            method: 'POST',
            headers: { 'Content-Type': 'application/json', ... },
            body: JSON.stringify({ username, password, display_name: displayName }),
        });
        const data = await res.json();
        if (!res.ok) return { success: false, error: data.error || 'Registration failed.' };
        // ... success path ...
    } catch {
        return { success: false, error: 'Network error. Please try again.' };  // LINE 178
    }
}
```

**Condition that triggers "Network error":** Only a **JavaScript exception** in the try block (e.g., JSON parse failure, fetch network failure, CORS error). Non-2xx HTTP responses are handled gracefully—the code extracts `data.error` from the JSON response and returns it. The "Network error" message fires ONLY on a true exception, not on a 400/409 from the server.

**Form submission handler (lines 1229–1273):**
- Gets trimmed username from input: `username = modal.querySelector('#auth-username')?.value.trim()`
- Calls `this.register(username, password, displayName)`
- Displays the returned error: `errorEl.textContent = result.error`

Therefore:
- If server returns `{"error": "Username must be at least..."}` with 400, the client displays that exact string.
- Only if the fetch throws an exception does "Network error. Please try again." appear.

---

**C. USERNAME VALIDATION**

**Server-side:** Spaces in usernames are **explicitly rejected** by the regex at line 862 of api.php. The input `"Ivan Woodman"` becomes `"ivan woodman"` after `mb_strtolower(trim())` and fails the pattern `/^[a-z0-9_.\-]+$/`, triggering the 400 error.

**Client-side:** The `<input>` field has no pattern, maxlength, or client-side validation. Spaces are accepted in the form and sent to the server.

---

**D. ACTIVITY LOG**

The server logs successful registrations (line 928, `logActivity('auth.register', ...)`), but **validation failures (username with space, short password, etc.) are NOT logged to tblActivityLog**—the handler just calls `sendJson()` and breaks. Only a successful registration creates an audit entry.

---

**THE ROOT CAUSE OF THE USER'S ISSUE**

When the user enters `"Ivan Woodman"` as the username:
1. Client trims it to `"Ivan Woodman"` and sends it as JSON to `auth_register`
2. Server lowercases and trims it: `"ivan woodman"`
3. Server regex `/^[a-z0-9_.\-]+$/` rejects the space
4. Server returns **HTTP 400 + JSON body: `{"error": "Username must be at least 3 characters (letters, numbers, _, -, . only)."}`**
5. Client receives 400 (not-ok), extracts `data.error`, displays it in the modal

**The user should see:** "Username must be at least 3 characters (letters, numbers, _, -, . only)."

**But they report seeing:** "Network error. Please try again."

This suggests either:
- The fetch is throwing an **exception** before hitting the JSON parse (CORS failure, network timeout, 0-byte response)
- The server is not returning a valid JSON body on the 400 (client's `res.json()` throws)
- An iOS Safari-specific issue is silently failing the request

The regex validation is correct and intentional—the real bug is why the error is not reaching the UI as the server error message.

 *
 * The iHymns API is a same-origin AJAX surface — every legitimate
 * caller is the SPA running on the same domain, talking to /api via
 * `fetch()` with `credentials: 'same-origin'`. There are no third-

 *   1. SameSite=Strict on the auth cookie — browsers refuse to send
 *      it on cross-site POST requests, so a CSRF attempt has no

 *   3. THIS guard: every POST must carry `X-Requested-With:
 *      XMLHttpRequest`. The header is a "forbidden header name" that

content.text:
I've got enough to act. Let me share my diagnosis with you before making the change.

## Diagnosis

The "Network error. Please try again." message in [user-auth.js:178](appWeb/public_html/js/modules/user-auth.js#L178) only fires when the `try {}` block **throws** — which means one of:
1. `fetch()` itself rejected (real network/CORS failure), OR
2. `res.json()` failed because the server returned **non-JSON** (HTML 500 page, empty body, plain text)

Since the client correctly handles structured JSON validation errors (with or without the space), and the user keeps seeing the same generic message, the most likely cause is **(2)**: something in `auth_register` is throwing an uncaught PHP error, and `api.php` has **no global exception handler** — uncaught throwables get the default PHP error page (HTML), which the client can't parse.

I can't see server logs from here to find the exact PHP error, but the fix should be **two-pronged so this never recurs across any endpoint**:

1. **Server fix** (`api.php`): register a global exception/error handler that converts every uncaught throwable into a JSON 500 with a request id. Logged in full to error_log; on Alpha/Beta the message + class are included in the JSON body so devs can see the real error in the browser. Production gets a generic message + the request id for log lookup.

2. **Client fix** (`user-auth.js`): when `res.json()` fails, fall back to `res.text()` and surface a more diagnostic message (HTTP status + first chunk of body) instead of the misleading "Network error".

These together will both **surface the real reason for the user's signup failure on next attempt** AND **prevent every other endpoint from masking errors the same way**.

Let me open the issue first, then implement.

input.command:
gh issue create --repo MWBMPartners/iHymns --title "Sign-up shows 'Network error. Please try again.' instead of the real reason" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

A user reported that creating a new account on **dev.ihymns.app** (alpha, build `v0.50.0` / `20260502212710`) fails with the unhelpful message **"Network error. Please try again."** on iOS Safari. Reproduced with both an invalid username (containing a space) and a valid one — the message is the same in both cases.

## Trace

1. Client `register()` in [appWeb/public_html/js/modules/user-auth.js:161](appWeb/public_html/js/modules/user-auth.js#L161) `POST`s JSON to `?action=auth_register`.
2. The "Network error" string at line 178 is emitted **only** when the `try {}` block throws — i.e. either `fetch()` rejected or `res.json()` rejected.
3. The server handler at [appWeb/public_html/api.php:791](appWeb/public_html/api.php#L791) returns proper JSON for known validation errors (400 / 409 / 429), and the client correctly extracts `data.error` for those — so this is **not** a validation failure path.
4. Therefore something downstream is throwing an uncaught PHP error and api.php has **no global exception handler** — uncaught throwables get the default PHP error page (HTML), which `res.json()` can't parse, the client falls into the catch, and the generic "Network error" surfaces.

## Underlying class of bug

This affects **every** `/api.php` endpoint, not just signup. Any uncaught `\Throwable` anywhere in the dispatch produces an HTML response that every client parses as a network failure, masking the real problem.

## Proposed fix

Two-pronged so this never recurs across any endpoint:

1. **Server (`api.php`)** — register a top-of-file exception/error handler that converts every uncaught throwable into a JSON `500` body with a request id. Logged in full to `error_log`. On Alpha/Beta the message + class go into the JSON body; production gets a generic message + the request id for log lookup.

2. **Client (`user-auth.js`)** — when `res.json()` fails, fall back to `res.text()` and include the HTTP status + first chunk of body in the displayed message. The "Network error" wording is reserved for the case where `fetch` itself rejected.

PR follows.

## Symptom screenshot

User submitted screenshot (omitted here for privacy). Inputs:
- Display Name: Ivan Woodman
- Username: Ivan Woodman (and also tried with the space removed — same error)
- Password: ~24 chars
EOF

## Summary

A new user reported that creating an account on `dev.ihymns.app` fails with the unhelpful **"Network error. Please try again."** — even after they fix the obvious problem (a space in the username) and try again.

The wording is wrong. The network is fine. The real cause is masked because:

1. The server has **no global exception handler** in `api.php`. Any uncaught `\Throwable` produces PHP's default HTML error page.
2. The client's `register()` / `login()` calls `res.json()` on the response. The HTML body throws a parse error, the catch block fires, and the catch hard-codes \"Network error\".

This affects **every** `/api.php` endpoint, not just signup.

Closes **#803**.

## What's in this PR

### Server — `appWeb/public_html/api.php`

Top-of-file global handler registered as early as possible (right after `infoAppVer.php` so we know the deployment channel). Two pieces working together:

- `set_exception_handler` — catches uncaught `\Throwable`
- `register_shutdown_function` + `error_get_last()` — catches PHP fatals (parse errors, OOM, …) that don't surface as throwables

Each uncaught error is logged to `error_log` with a 10-char `request_id` correlation token. The HTTP response branches by request type:

- **Action requests** (`?action=…`) → JSON 500 with `error`, `request_id`. On Alpha/Beta the body also includes `exception_class` + the file:line `where` so devs can debug from the browser. Production gets a generic `\"Internal server error.\"` + `request_id` only.
- **Page requests** (`?page=…`) → HTML alert chunk (the SPA injects HTML responses) with the same env-gated detail policy.

### Client — `appWeb/public_html/js/modules/user-auth.js`

`register()` and `login()` now share a new `_postJson()` helper that distinguishes three failure modes that previously all collapsed to \"Network error\":

| Symptom | Old message | New message |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `fetch()` rejected (real connectivity / CORS) | \"Network error. Please try again.\" | \"Network error. Please check your connection and try again.\" |
| `res.json()` failed (server returned non-JSON) | \"Network error. Please try again.\" | \"Server returned an unreadable response (HTTP 500 Internal Server Error). Server said: \\\"<first 200 chars of body>\\\". This is a server bug — please report it.\" |
| `res.ok === false` with JSON body | (already used `data.error`) | Same, plus `[ref abc1234567]` appended when `request_id` is present |

## Why this is the right fix

I can't see server logs from the dev box, so I don't know which specific PHP error is firing inside `auth_register` on `dev.ihymns.app` right now. With this PR merged, the actual exception class + message + file:line will surface in the modal on the user's next attempt (via the Alpha/Beta verbose body). At that point the underlying root cause becomes a one-liner to fix.

Even more importantly, **every other API endpoint** picks up the same protection — no more silent \"Network error\" lies.

## Files

| File | Change |
| --- | --- |
| `appWeb/public_html/api.php` | New global handler closure (~90 LOC) registered before the rest of the bootstrap requires. |
| `appWeb/public_html/js/modules/user-auth.js` | New `_postJson()` helper (~70 LOC); `register()` / `login()` rewritten to use it. |

## Test plan

- [ ] Deploy to alpha. Hit the Create Account modal with the same inputs as the original report — expect the real PHP error message + `[ref ...]` token in the modal instead of \"Network error\".
- [ ] Same flow on Login — expect the same improved error treatment.
- [ ] Trigger a true network failure (kill DNS / disconnect WiFi) — expect \"Network error. Please check your connection and try again.\"
- [ ] In a `php -l` smoke test, hit `/api.php?action=throw_test` (you'd need to add a temporary throw in a case to verify) — expect a JSON 500 with `error` + `request_id` + `exception_class` (since alpha is verbose).
- [ ] Check `error_log` has the corresponding `[api uncaught rid=…]` line so the curator can correlate browser → log.
- [ ] On a production deployment (Status = NULL) — expect the JSON body to have the generic \"Internal server error.\" string only, not the exception class / message. (Verbose mode is gated by `Alpha`/`Beta` env detection from `infoAppVer.php`.)

## Refs

- Closes #803.
- The signup endpoint itself isn't changed — its actual server-side error will become visible to the user on next attempt and can be addressed in a follow-up issue once we see the message.

🤖 Generated with [Claude Code](https://claude.com/claude-code)
EOF

"file": "api.php"

input.command:
gh issue create --repo MWBMPartners/iHymns --title "Activity Log 'When' column should show visitor's local time, not server's" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Symptom

The Activity Log viewer at `/manage/activity-log` displays the **When** column in what looks like the server's wall-clock time, not the curator's browser-local time. PR #724 (#723) was meant to convert to local time, but the conversion silently no-ops when the server's MySQL session timezone isn't UTC — the data attribute the JS reads claims to be UTC (`Z` suffix) but is actually the session-local string MySQL returned.

## Trace

The viewer renders each cell as:

```php
data-utc="<?= str_replace(' ', 'T', (string)$r['CreatedAt']) . 'Z' ?>"
```

`tblActivityLog.CreatedAt` is a `TIMESTAMP` column — MySQL stores it in UTC but returns it converted to the session timezone (`SYSTEM` by default = OS timezone). Suffixing `Z` claims the value is UTC, but if the server's TZ isn't UTC the claim is a lie. The JS then parses as UTC and applies the visitor's offset on top — producing a doubly-wrong value, OR appearing correct only when visitor and server are in the same TZ.

The CSV export has the same problem — it dumps the raw `CreatedAt` value with no timezone marker.

## Goal

- The **When** column should display the **visitor's local time** (not the server's), regardless of what timezone the MySQL server, PHP server, or curator's browser is in.
- If the visitor's timezone can't be determined (very old browser, missing `Intl`), fall back to **UTC** with a clear `UTC` suffix in the cell so the value is unambiguous.
- The CSV export should be unambiguous too — emit an explicit UTC ISO column.

## Fix outline

1. SELECT additionally emits `UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.CreatedAt) AS CreatedAtTs` — Unix timestamps are seconds since epoch in UTC, no session-TZ ambiguity.
2. Cell-text rendering uses `gmdate('Y-m-d H:i:s', $ts) . ' UTC'` so the fallback path always shows a correct UTC value.
3. The data attribute carries the Unix timestamp (`data-ts`) instead of the unreliable `data-utc` string.
4. JS reads `data-ts`, converts to a `Date` via `* 1000`, and formats via `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, …)` (resolves to the visitor's locale + timezone). Header label flips to `When (local)`.
5. CSV export gets a new `CreatedAtUtc` column with the same `gmdate()` UTC ISO so downloaded reports are TZ-unambiguous.

PR follows.
EOF
)" --label bug 2>&1 | tail -3

<!-- Local-time conversion + UA-wrap styling (#721 / #723).
         Each .activity-when cell carries data-utc="2026-04-30T13:53:42Z";
         this script formats it via the browser's Intl.DateTimeFormat in
         the user's local timezone and replaces the cell's text. If Intl
         isn't available (very old browser) the cells stay UTC and the
         header label stays "When (UTC)". -->
    <style>
        .activity-ua {
            display: inline-block;
            max-width: 100%;
            word-break: break-word;
            overflow-wrap: anywhere;
        }
    </style>
    <script>
    (function () {
        try {
            if (typeof Intl === 'undefined' || !Intl.DateTimeFormat) return;
            var fmt = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {
                year:   'numeric', month:  '2-digit', day:    '2-digit',
                hour:   '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', second: '2-digit',
                hour12: false,
            });
            var cells = document.querySelectorAll('.activity-when[data-utc]');
            if (!cells.length) return;
            cells.forEach(function (cell) {
                var iso = cell.getAttribute('data-utc');
                if (!iso) return;
                var d = new Date(iso);
                if (isNaN(d.getTime())) return;
                /* Reformat to "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" — matches the
                   table's existing visual cadence; some locales would
                   otherwise produce "30/04/2026, 14:53:42" which jars
                   in a tabular layout. */
                var parts = fmt.formatToParts(d).reduce(function (acc, p) {
                    if (p.type !== 'literal') acc[p.type] = p.value; return acc;
                }, {});
                cell.textContent = parts.year + '-' + parts.month + '-' + parts.day
                    + ' ' + parts.hour + ':' + parts.minute + ':' + parts.second;
            });
            var header = document.getElementById('activity-when-header');
            if (header) header.textContent = 'When (local)';
        } catch (_e) { /* fail-soft — leave UTC text in place */ }
    })();
    </script>

<!-- Visitor-local time conversion (#805, replaces #721 / #723).
         Each .activity-when cell carries data-ts="<unix-seconds-utc>";
         this script multiplies by 1000, builds a Date, formats via the
         browser's Intl.DateTimeFormat in the visitor's resolved
         timezone, and replaces the cell's text. The fallback (cell
         text rendered server-side as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC` from
         gmdate(UNIX_TIMESTAMP)) stays in place if Intl is unavailable
         OR the visitor's TZ can't be resolved — so the column is
         always either visitor-local or unambiguous UTC, never silently
         server-local-pretending-to-be-anything-else. -->
    <style>
        .activity-ua {
            display: inline-block;
            max-width: 100%;
            word-break: break-word;
            overflow-wrap: anywhere;
        }
    </style>
    <script>
    (function () {
        try {
            if (typeof Intl === 'undefined' || !Intl.DateTimeFormat) return;
            /* Resolve the visitor's TZ explicitly so we can fall back
               to UTC display if it comes back empty (some locked-down
               browser configs return ''). */
            var resolved = Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions();
            var visitorTz = resolved && resolved.timeZone ? resolved.timeZone : '';
            if (!visitorTz) return; /* fall back to server-rendered UTC */
            var fmt = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, {
                year:    'numeric', month:  '2-digit', day:    '2-digit',
                hour:    '2-digit', minute: '2-digit', second: '2-digit',
                hour12:  false,
                timeZone: visitorTz,
            });
            var cells = document.querySelectorAll('.activity-when[data-ts]');
            if (!cells.length) return;
            cells.forEach(function (cell) {
                var ts = parseInt(cell.getAttribute('data-ts') || '0', 10);
                if (!ts) return;
                var d = new Date(ts * 1000);
                if (isNaN(d.getTime())) return;
                /* Reformat to "YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS" — matches the
                   table's existing visual cadence; some locales would
                   otherwise produce "30/04/2026, 14:53:42" which jars
                   in a tabular layout. */
                var parts = fmt.formatToParts(d).reduce(function (acc, p) {
                    if (p.type !== 'literal') acc[p.type] = p.value; return acc;
                }, {});
                cell.textContent = parts.year + '-' + parts.month + '-' + parts.day
                    + ' ' + parts.hour + ':' + parts.minute + ':' + parts.second;
                /* Hover title carries the resolved timezone name so
                   curators inspecting an entry can see the offset
                   they're looking at — useful when comparing logs
                   across teammates in different regions. */
                cell.setAttribute('title', cell.textContent + ' (' + visitorTz + ')');
            });
            var header = document.getElementById('activity-when-header');
            if (header) header.textContent = 'When (local — ' + visitorTz + ')';
        } catch (_e) { /* fail-soft — server-rendered UTC stays */ }
    })();
    </script>

attribute it read claimed UTC (suffix 'Z') while actually carrying
whatever string MySQL returned for the TIMESTAMP column. With the
default `SYSTEM` session TZ, that string is the server's wall
clock — so the JS treated server-local as UTC and applied the
visitor's offset on top, producing a doubly-wrong result OR
appearing correct only when visitor and server happen to share a
timezone.

    pull `UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.CreatedAt) AS CreatedAtTs`. Unix
    timestamps are seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC by
    definition — no MySQL session TZ ambiguity, no PHP
    date.timezone interaction.

    Each cell is rendered server-side as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC`
    via gmdate(CreatedAtTs) so the fallback (no JS / no Intl)
    shows a correct, clearly-labelled UTC value.

    The cell carries `data-ts="<seconds>"` instead of the
    misleading `data-utc` ISO string.

  Client (inline JS in the same file)

    UTC if either Intl is missing or the resolved TZ is empty.
    When present, formats the cell via

    the header to "When (local — Europe/London)" or whatever the
    resolved IANA name is. Hover title carries the formatted time

  CSV export

    in ISO-8601 form ("2026-05-02T16:51:18Z"). Legacy `CreatedAt`
    column preserved for back-compat with any existing report

Closes #805.

cd /tmp/ihymns-tz && gh pr create --base alpha --title "fix(activity-log): show visitor's local time, not server's (#805)" --body "$(cat <<'EOF'
## Summary

PR #724 (#723) added a JS converter that was meant to display each row's `CreatedAt` in the **visitor's** local timezone, but the data attribute it read claimed UTC (suffix `Z`) while actually carrying whatever string MySQL returned for the `TIMESTAMP` column. With the default `SYSTEM` session TZ that string is the **server's** wall clock — so the JS treated server-local as UTC and applied the visitor's offset on top, producing a doubly-wrong result OR appearing correct only when visitor and server happen to share a timezone.

Closes **#805**.

## What's in this PR

### Server (`appWeb/public_html/manage/activity-log.php`)

Both the paginated SELECT and the CSV-export SELECT now also pull `UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.CreatedAt) AS CreatedAtTs`. Unix timestamps are seconds since 1970-01-01 00:00:00 UTC by definition — no MySQL session TZ ambiguity, no PHP `date.timezone` interaction.

Each cell is rendered server-side as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC` via `gmdate(CreatedAtTs)` so the fallback (no JS / no Intl) shows a correct, clearly-labelled UTC value.

The cell carries `data-ts=\"<seconds>\"` instead of the misleading `data-utc` ISO string.

### Client (inline JS in the same file)

Resolves the visitor's TZ via `Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`. Falls back to the server-rendered UTC if either `Intl` is missing or the resolved TZ is empty. When present, formats the cell via `Intl.DateTimeFormat(undefined, { …, timeZone: visitorTz })` and replaces the cell text, drops the \" UTC\" suffix, and flips the header to `When (local — Europe/London)` or whatever the resolved IANA name is. Hover title carries the formatted time + the resolved zone for cross-team correlation.

### CSV export

New `CreatedAtUtc` column populated from `gmdate(CreatedAtTs)` in ISO-8601 form (`2026-05-02T16:51:18Z`). Legacy `CreatedAt` column preserved for back-compat with any existing report tooling but is now considered deprecated — `CreatedAtUtc` is the canonical timestamp.

## Why this is robust

The previous bug was a quiet one — visible only when visitor TZ ≠ server TZ. The new design **eliminates the timezone ambiguity at the source**:

| Path | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Cell data attribute | `data-utc=\"<server-local-string-with-Z\"` (lie) | `data-ts=\"<unix-seconds-utc>\"` (true by definition) |
| Cell fallback text | server-local string (no TZ marker) | `<UTC string> UTC` (clearly UTC, correct under any server TZ) |
| JS conversion target | undefined / browser default | explicit visitor-resolved IANA TZ |
| When visitor TZ is unresolvable | silent (cells stay as misleading server-local) | falls back to UTC (clearly labelled) |
| CSV download | server-local string (no TZ marker) | new `CreatedAtUtc` ISO-8601 column |

## Files

content.text:
Two PRs out:

**[#804](https://github.com/MWBMPartners/iHymns/pull/804) — fix(api,auth): surface real signup/login errors instead of "Network error"** — already merged (`63e0b5d`). This is what made your activity-log error visible. Two commits:
1. Global JSON error handler in `api.php` — every uncaught throwable now lands as JSON 500 with a request id, instead of an HTML error page that the client misreports as "Network error".
2. Removed the dead `UserId` query in `auth_register` — the real root cause of your signup failure. The leftover `SELECT … UserId FROM tblLoginAttempts …` referenced a column that doesn't exist on that table (schema is `Id, IpAddress, Username, Success, AttemptedAt`). mysqli with strict mode threw on every signup attempt. The code's own comment claimed it was "no-op leftover" — but mysqli does NOT silently no-op. Sign-up should now work.

**[#806](https://github.com/MWBMPartners/iHymns/pull/806) — fix(activity-log): show visitor's local time, not server's** — addresses your second point. Three changes:
- The SELECTs (paginated + CSV) now also pull `UNIX_TIMESTAMP(a.CreatedAt)`. Unix timestamps are seconds-since-epoch UTC by definition — no MySQL session TZ ambiguity.
- Cells render server-side as `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS UTC` via `gmdate()` — the fallback (no JS) is now always correct + clearly labelled.
- JS resolves the visitor's TZ explicitly (`Intl.DateTimeFormat().resolvedOptions().timeZone`) and formats with `timeZone: visitorTz`. Header flips to `When (local — Europe/London)` (or whatever the resolved IANA name is). When TZ can't be resolved, the UTC fallback stays.
- CSV export gains a `CreatedAtUtc` column (`2026-05-02T16:51:18Z`) so downloaded reports are TZ-unambiguous too.

After #806 merges + deploys, retry signup on dev.ihymns.app — with #804 already live, if anything else fires you'll see the actual exception message + a `[ref ...]` token tied to the activity log row, rather than "Network error".

Worktrees at `/tmp/ihymns-signup`, `/tmp/ihymns-tz` left in place; I can clean them up after #806 merges.
